incident: Root filesystem exhausted during duplicate node image imports and an initial Spark image export.
observed_effects: Git object writes temporarily failed; source files stayed intact in isolated /tmp worktrees.
PostgreSQL entered automatic recovery and the receiver logged transient scrape errors.
Java JFR terminated when its temporary recording could not be written.
Some Collector forwarding log records were truncated; bounded capture counts malformed records explicitly.
recovery: Archived completed PoC host images under /tmp/ddot-preserved-images before removing redundant host tags; running kind worker images remained available.
Pruned only explicitly selected unused cache records from this PoC and the retired fake-backend build.
Removed unused ddot image copies from the control-plane node after verifying all PoC pods were on the worker; future imports target only the worker.
Changed Java profiling temporary files to a bounded 256Mi memory-backed volume with explicit JVM heap and container memory limits.
Optimized Spark build to avoid recursive chmod copying its large layer, exported the image to a /tmp Docker archive, reclaimed its completed build cache, then imported only into the worker.
Preserved default Go and Bazel caches in /tmp with original-path symlinks; these initial preservation attempts did not recover root capacity.
preserved: Unrelated workloads, images, persistent volumes, user source repositories and original checkout work were preserved.
verification: Fresh CI and DSM Jobs and a new bounded Collector observation window supersede missing earlier route counts. Historical DBM correlation is retained; fresh full record readback is not claimed.
